intended_use: A check of the method on public data with real outcomes. This model is not for scoring anyone: it shows how the same pipeline does where the outcomes are known.

metrics.measured_on: validation period (the held-back test period is not used here)
metrics.split: at random, keeping the same share of repaid loans in each part
metrics.split_note: Weaker split: this data source has no usable dates, so loans were divided at random (keeping the same share of repaid loans in each part) instead of by time.
metrics.inputs: Of the last six months in which the card was used, the share with no late payment | The longest payment delay, in months, in the last six months | The payment delay, in months, in the most recent month | Amount paid in five months divided by the bills of the month before each | Average bill over six months divided by the credit limit | Newest bill minus oldest bill, divided by the credit limit | Of the months that followed a bill, the share in which nothing was paid
metrics.simpler_model: only whether the most recent monthly bill was paid late
metrics.data_source: UCI 'default of credit card clients': 30,000 credit-card clients in Taiwan, 2005 (I-Cheng Yeh, 2009)
metrics.terms: CC BY 4.0, as stated on the UCI page
metrics.label: Repaid: the client did not default on the next month's payment
metrics.banner: Public data: Taiwan credit cards, not ShopUp data. Decision support only.
metrics.what_this_shows: Inputs describing how a client paid over six months rank real outcomes well, and the bands separate repaid from not repaid.
metrics.what_this_does_not_show: Anything about merchants: these are consumer credit cards in Taiwan in 2005. The split is random, not by time, so the result is somewhat easier than a real forward test.
metrics.group_findings: No group gap was flagged on these data.

limitations: Public data, not ShopUp data. It tests the method on real payment behaviour, not on merchants.
Labels exist only for people who received credit before. The model may not work for applicants who would have been turned down under earlier policy.
Scores are less certain when coverage is low. A thin file is never treated as a bad file: below the coverage line the band is 'Needs more info', whatever the score.
The numbers above are from the validation period. It was also used to choose the model and the calibration, so they are a little optimistic.
Group columns are used only to audit results, never as model inputs. The group audit shows where the model works measurably differently on these data; it does not show that the model is fair.
The tool supports a human decision. It must not be used for automatic approval or decline.
